description:
## Contract risk

RFC 8620 §5.4 defines /copy with these standard optional arguments:

- `ifFromInState`: 'String|null'      — guard against concurrent change at source
- `ifInState`:     'String|null'      — guard against concurrent change at target
- `onSuccessDestroyOriginal`: 'Boolean' (default false)
- `destroyFromIfInState`:     'String|null' — guards the implied source destroy

Canonical mail-client exposes them via `EmailCopyParams` at
crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/mod.rs:67-84:

```rust
pub struct EmailCopyParams {
    pub from_account_id: Id,
    pub on_success_destroy_original: Option<bool>,
    pub destroy_from_if_in_state: Option<jmap_types::State>,
    pub extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
}
```

(Note: this canonical struct itself doesn't expose `ifFromInState` or
`ifInState` either — that's a separate canonical gap, not in scope for this
finding. But the workspace canonical at least carries
`onSuccessDestroyOriginal` and `destroyFromIfInState`.)

calendars-client `calendar_event_copy` at
crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/event_copy.rs:22-26 takes:

```rust
pub async fn calendar_event_copy(
    &self,
    from_account_id: &Id,
    create: HashMap<String, jmap_calendars_types::CalendarEvent>,
) -> ...
```

Two arguments. No `onSuccessDestroyOriginal`, no `destroyFromIfInState`, no
`ifFromInState`, no `ifInState`.

## Why this matters for a caller

A caller copying a calendar event from a colleague's shared account into
their own with the intent 'and remove the original after successful copy'
(the classic 'move' operation, which JMAP /copy implements via the
`onSuccessDestroyOriginal` flag) has no path through this client. They
must either fork or write a two-call sequence (/copy, then /set destroy
against the source account), losing atomicity.

Similarly for state-conditional copy. A caller who fetched the source event
at state s5 and wants to copy only if source is still at s5 cannot express
this through the API. They must accept the risk that the source event was
modified between read and copy.

## What goes wrong if this stays

Real callability gap. JMAP /copy without `onSuccessDestroyOriginal` is half
the standard /copy primitive — the other half (move-by-copy-then-destroy as
a single atomic operation) is unreachable.

Once shipped at 0.x.y, adding these as a `CalendarEventCopyParams` struct
or as additional arguments is a breaking change.

## Fix shape

Introduce `CalendarEventCopyParams` mirroring mail-client's `EmailCopyParams`:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, serde::Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct CalendarEventCopyParams {
    pub from_account_id: Id,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub on_success_destroy_original: Option<bool>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub destroy_from_if_in_state: Option<jmap_types::State>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub if_from_in_state: Option<jmap_types::State>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub if_in_state: Option<jmap_types::State>,
    #[serde(flatten, default, skip_serializing_if = "serde_json::Map::is_empty")]
    pub extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
}
```

The signature becomes:

```rust
pub async fn calendar_event_copy(
    &self,
    params: CalendarEventCopyParams,
    create: HashMap<String, CalendarEvent>,
) -> Result<SetResponse<CalendarEvent>, ClientError>
```

This also fixes the workspace canonical gap (mail-client's `EmailCopyParams`
is itself missing `ifFromInState` and `ifInState`); if accepted, sweep
mail-client first, then propagate per the canonical-template rule.
